parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
An object travels in a circle at constant speed.

State the names of two quantities that vary during the motion of the object.

markscheme_points.text: any 2 points from: • (angular) displacement • velocity • momentum • (centripetal) acceleration • (resultant) force

hints: Hint 1: Speed is constant, but think carefully about scalars versus vectors - which type of quantity can change even if its magnitude stays the same?
Hint 2: Focus on quantities whose direction is tied to the motion around the circle, such as the direction of travel and the direction pointing toward the centre.
parts.proper_answer: Any two from: velocity, momentum, (centripetal) acceleration, (resultant / centripetal) force, (angular) displacement.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Separate Speed from Velocity**
You are told the speed is constant. Speed is a scalar with magnitude only, so it does not vary. Velocity is a vector, so it has magnitude and direction. In circular motion the direction of travel is continuously changing, so velocity must be changing even though speed is fixed.

Step 2: **Follow the Other Vectors**
Any vector that depends on velocity or its direction also changes. That includes momentum $p = mv$, centripetal acceleration $a = v^2/r$ directed to the centre, and resultant force $F = ma$ directed to the centre. Angular displacement around the circle also increases. Any two of these are valid answers, e.g. velocity and centripetal acceleration.

parts.label: (b)
parts.part_stem:
A charged particle of mass $m$ and with charge $q$ enters a region of uniform magnetic field, perpendicular to the field lines. The magnetic flux density is $B$.

The particle travels in a circle with period $T$ and radius $r$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
By considering the magnetic force acting on the particle, show that
$$B = \frac{2\pi m}{qT}.$$

markscheme_points.text: completion of algebra leading to B = 2πm / qT

hints: Hint 1: Start by thinking about what keeps the charged particle moving in a circle - which magnetic force acts as the centripetal force toward the centre?
Hint 2: Recall how orbital speed $v$ is linked to one full circumference and the time for one orbit, the period $T$.
Hint 3: Combine your two equations to eliminate both $v$ and $r$, then rearrange to make $B$ the subject.
parts.proper_answer: $Bqv = mv^{2}/r$ with $v = 2\pi r/T$ gives $Bq = m(2\pi r/T)/r = 2\pi m/T$, so $B = 2\pi m/qT$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Magnetic Force Provides Centripetal Force**
The particle enters perpendicular to the field, so the magnetic force magnitude is $$F_B = Bqv$$ This force acts perpendicular to velocity at all times, so it does no work but bends the path into a circle. It must supply the required centripetal force: $$F_c = \frac{mv^2}{r}$$ Equating them: $$Bqv = \frac{mv^2}{r}$$

Step 2: **Express Speed Using Period**
In one period $T$ the particle travels one circumference $2\pi r$. So at constant speed: $$v = \frac{2\pi r}{T}$$

Step 3: **Eliminate v and r**
Cancel one $v$ from the force equation: $$Bq = \frac{mv}{r}$$ Substitute $v$: $$Bq = \frac{m}{r} \times \frac{2\pi r}{T} = \frac{2\pi m}{T}$$ The radius $r$ cancels, showing $T$ is independent of $r$. Rearranging: $$B = \frac{2\pi m}{qT}$$ as required.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The particle is an alpha particle. The period of the circular motion is $2.5\,\mu\text{s}$.

Calculate $B$.
hints: Hint 1: Recall what an alpha particle is made of to get $m$ and $q$ - how many proton masses and how many elementary charges does it carry?
Hint 2: Check your period conversion from $\mu\text{s}$ to $\text{s}$ and then substitute all SI values into the formula from (b)(i).
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify m and q for Alpha Particle**
An alpha particle is a helium nucleus: 2 protons + 2 neutrons. So mass $m \approx 4u = 4 \times 1.66 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}$ and charge $q = 2e = 2 \times 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$. Period $T = 2.5\,\mu\text{s} = 2.5 \times 10^{-6}\text{ s}$.

Step 2: **Substitute into B Formula**
$$B = \frac{2\pi m}{qT} = \frac{2\pi \times 4 \times 1.66 \times 10^{-27}}{2 \times 1.60 \times 10^{-19} \times 2.5 \times 10^{-6}}$$ $$B \approx 0.052\text{ T}$$ to 2 s.f.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
A second alpha particle is in the same uniform field. It travels in a circle of radius $2r$.

State and explain how the periods of the motion of the two particles compare.

markscheme_points.text: either the same because T is independent of r or the same because B, q and m are unchanged or the same because both radius and speed have doubled

hints: Hint 1: Look back at the formula $B = 2\pi m/qT$ - which variables does $T$ depend on, and does radius $r$ appear in it?
parts.proper_answer: Periods are the same. $T$ is independent of $r$ (and $v$) since $B$, $q$ and $m$ are unchanged.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Use the Period Formula**
Rearranged, $T = 2\pi m / Bq$. For the same particle in the same field, $m$, $q$ and $B$ are all unchanged, so $T$ is unchanged. Physically, a larger radius $2r$ needs double the speed, so the time for one orbit stays the same. Hence the periods are equal.

key_concepts: period independent of radius and speed
isochronous nature of magnetic circular motion

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
The speed of the alpha particle in (b)(ii) is $1.1 \times 10^6\,\text{m s}^{-1}$. An electric field is applied so that this particle now moves with constant velocity.

Use your answer in (b)(ii) to calculate the electric field strength $E$. Give the unit with your answer.
hints: Hint 1: For constant velocity the resultant force must be zero - think about which two opposing forces must balance in magnitude.
Hint 2: Cancel the common charge and use your $B$ value from (b)(ii) with the given speed to find $E$, remembering to add the correct unit.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Balance Forces for Straight Motion**
Constant velocity means zero resultant force. The electric force $F_E = qE$ must exactly cancel the magnetic force $F_B = Bqv$ in magnitude: $$qE = Bqv$$ The charge $q$ cancels to give the velocity-selector result: $$E = Bv$$

Step 2: **Calculate E**
Using $B = 0.052\text{ T}$ and $v = 1.1 \times 10^{6}\text{ m s}^{-1}$: $$E = 0.052 \times 1.1 \times 10^{6} \approx 5.7 \times 10^{4}\text{ V m}^{-1}$$ Unit $\text{V m}^{-1}$ is equivalent to $\text{N C}^{-1}$.
